Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.inspector_comments: THE FRONT FASCADE (EAST ELEVATION) OF THIS BUILDING IS COMPRISED OF BRICK, STONE AND METAL ELEMENTS. *METAL ORNEMENTAL TRIM ELEMENTS ... THERE ARE 2 BAY WINDOWED WALLS FROM THE 2CD THROUGH THE 3RD FLOORS AND UP TO AND BEYOND THE ROOFLINE. THE MEALWORK IS SEVERELY RUSTED / PITTED WITH HOLES AT VARIOUS LOCATIONS. THE METALWORK IN SOME AREAS IS SO DEGRADED THAT IT HAS CORRODED TO THE POINT OF LOOSE METAL FLAKES. THERE ARE ALSO METAL TRIM COMPONENTS THAT ARE NOT FIRMLY ATTACHED TO THE BUILDING'S STRUCTURE. A PORTION OF THIS METALWORK HAS BEEN COVERED WITH PLASTIC MESH NETTING IN AN ATTEMPT TO ABATE THE DANGEROUS AND HAZARDOUS CONDITION OF SOME OF THE MORE CORRODED METALWORK. THIS PLASTIC MESH NETTING WAS UNPROFESSIONALLY INSTALLED AND DOES NOT COMPLETELY OR SECURELY COVER THE AFFECTED METAL ELEMENTS THAT ARE LOOSE / DETACHED FROM THE BUILDING'S STRUCTURE.*STONEWORK ... THERE IS A LARGE SPALL ABOVE THE 3354 ENTRANCE DOOR. THIS FRACTURED PIECE OF STONE IS DETACHED AND A HAZARD EXISTS IF IT WERE TO BECOME COMPLETELY DETACHED. *BRICKWORK ... A LARGE SIGN / FLEXIBLE BANNER COVERS ALL OF THE BRICKWORK OF THIS EAST ELEVATION. UNABLE TO INSPECT. *BANNER / SIGN ... THIS 25'X25' BANNER WAS POORLY INSTALLED WITHOUT PERMIT. EVEN A LIGHT LIGHT CAUSES THIS HUGE, HEAVY BANNER TO FLUTTER EXCESSIVELY. INCLUDED IN THE FASTENING METHOD ARE MAKE SHIFT ROPE AND BUNGIE TYPE CORD ATTACHMENT POINTS FOR THE BANNER TO THE BUILDING STRUCTURE. THERE IS A HAZARD OF THIS HEAVY BANNER BECOMING COMPLETELY DETACHED IN HIGH WIND CONDITIONS.THE ELEMENTS OF THIS EAST ELEVATION ARE TO BE, AS A WHOLE, CONSIDERED DANGEROUS AND HAZARDOUS. THIS IS A HIGH TRAFFIC PEDESTRIAN COMMERCIAL CORRIDOR. PLANS AND PERMIT ARE REQUIRED FOR REPAIRS.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.inspector_comments: THIS 1ST FLOOR COMMERCIAL MERCHANTILE SPACE IS BEING OPERATED AS A MASSAGE PARLOR WITH A REGULATED BUSINESS LICENSE. THIS IS CONSIDERED A CHANGE OF USE FOR THIS SPACE AND THIS CHANGE OF USE MUST BE REFECTED IN THE ARCHITECTURAL PLANS TO BE SUBMITTED TO THE DEPARTMENT OF BUILDINGS. THESE PLANS MUST INCLUDE THE ADDITION OF THE PROPER SANITARY FACILITIES THAT ARE CODE COMPLIANT. THERE ARE NO PLANS ON FILE FOR THE CHANGE FROM A MERCHANTILE SPACE TO THE CURRENT SPECIAL USE LICENSED OPERATION.ALSO, THIS 1ST FLOOR SPACE HAS BEEN REHABBED WITH NEW ELECTRICAL / PLUMBING PIPING AND FIXTURES AS WELL AS THE ADDITION OF SEVERAL PARTITION WALLS FORMING VARIOUS MASSAGE ROOMS AND A SLEEPING ROOM. A FURNACE AND ASSOCIATED DUCTWORK HAS ALSO BEEN INSTALLED WITHOUT PERMIT.ALSO, A KITCHEN AND FULL BATHROOM HAVE BEEN INSTALLED. ALSO, A SLEEPING ROOM IS IN USE WITH A BED / BEDDING, CLOSET WITH CLOTHING, A DRESSER WITH CLOTHING AND OTHER PERSONAL ITEMS INDICATING THIS IS AN "IN USE" DWELLING UNIT. THERE ARE NO PLANS OR PERMITS ON FILE FOR THIS REHAB OR THE CURRENT USE AS A DWELLING UNIT.THIS WAS A TASK FORCE INSPECTION WITH BACP, DOB AND CPD VICE. BACP ISSUED NUMEROUS TICKETS BASED ON INFRACTIONS OF THE CURRENT REGULATED BUSINESS LICENSE. THIS COMPLAINT ORIGINATED WITH CHICAGO POLICE VICE UNIT BASED ON NUMEROUS NEIGHBORHOOD COMPLAINTS ABOUT ILLEGAL ACTIVITY AT THIS ESTABLISHMENT. AT THE TIME OF THIS INSPECTION (9PM SATURDAY NIGHT) THERE WAS 1 FEMALE MASSEUSE AND 3 CUSTOMERS IN FRONT WAITING FOR SERVICE. A 4TH CUSTOMER, A MALE, IN THE REAR MASSAGE ROOM, RAN OUT THE BACK DOOR PARTIALLY CLOTHED AFTER THE MASSEUSE CALLED TO THIS CUSTOMER VOCALLY THAT THE POLICE WERE PRESENT.A DOB CLOSURE ORDER IS IN EFFECT.SECTION 14A-4-401.1.

Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install one on any living level with a habitable room or unenclosed heating plant, on the uppermost ceiling of enclosed porch stairwell, and within 15 feet of every sleeping room. Be sure the detector is at least 4 inches from the wall, 4 to 12 inches from the ceiling, and not above door or window.
